chunks: First: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd from al-Qasim ibn Sulayman from Jarrah al-Mad'ai ni from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said:
The man should not drink while standing. The meaning in this report is a type of dislike (karahah) rather than prohibition (haram), which is indicated by this.
Second: What Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Fadalah ibn Ayyub from Ismail ibn Abi Ziyad from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
He said: Drinking while standing is stronger for you and more sound.

key_terms.كَرَاهِيَة: Dislike (a level below prohibition in Islamic jurisprudence)

ai.seo_question: Is drinking while standing forbidden or just disliked in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith explores the juristic distinction between drinking while standing, which is generally considered makruh (disliked) rather than haram, and the physiological benefits of the posture. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) highlights that standing aids digestion and strengthens the body, reflecting the Prophetic tradition of maintaining physical health as part of spiritual well-being. This ruling is often contextualized within the broader Islamic emphasis on moderation and avoiding habits that may lead to excess or health issues.
